DEP 4, written in 2015, set a feature release every eight months, the rhythm since 1.8, and, from 2.0, series of three, X.0, X.1 and X.2, the last its long-term release (`deps:final/0004-release-schedule.rst`).

The releases that were to be 7.0 and 7.1 are Django 2028 and Django 2029 (`deps:accepted/0020-annual-release-cycle.rst`, `docs/releases/6.2.txt`; [Django's version: `VersionTuple` and `get_version`](utils/version.md)).

This commit is main on 26 September 2026, a pre-alpha of 6.2 (`django/utils/version.py:get_version`); 6.1.1 is the newest release, and 6.2 is expected in April 2027.

The figure sets the releases in their years, from the release notes (`docs/releases/`) and, for [0.90](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2005/nov/16/firstrelease/), [0.96](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2007/mar/23/096/) and [1.0](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2008/sep/03/1/), the project's announcements: look for the long-term releases, the two changes of rhythm, and where this commit stands.

Since 6.1, reading a field or a related object a queryset did not load follows a **fetch mode**: `FETCH_ONE`, the old way, a query for that instance; `FETCH_PEERS`, which fetches it at once for that instance and its peers, other instances of its model that the same run of the queryset made; or `FETCH_RAISE`, which refuses (`django/db/models/fetch_modes.py`; [What changed in querysets](changes/querysets.md)).

**Safer defaults**: aware datetimes (5.0), 64-bit automatic keys (6.0), `"https"` as the scheme a form's URL field assumes (6.0), and more iterations of the PBKDF2 password hasher in every feature release (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:PBKDF2PasswordHasher`).
The release process allows a change outright where a path through deprecation is not possible or not worth its cost (`docs/internals/release-process.txt`).

The old behaviour stays for at least two feature releases and ordinarily warns, some of its warnings only when the use comes from outside Django's own code (`django/utils/deprecation.py:warn_about_external_use`).

`RemovedInDjango2028Warning` is a `DeprecationWarning`, which Python shows by default only when the line it names is in the script Python runs; `RemovedInDjango2029Warning` is a `PendingDeprecationWarning`, which Python never shows by default (`django/utils/deprecation.py`).

Some deprecations come with a **transitional setting**, which lets a project take the new behaviour early or keep the old one for a time: at this commit `URLIZE_ASSUME_HTTPS`, for `"https"` as the scheme `django.utils.html.urlize` assumes; `USE_BLANK_CHOICE_DASH`, for the old label of a form's blank choice; and `SIGNED_COOKIE_LEGACY_SALT_FALLBACK`, for a signed cookie's old salt (`django/conf/global_settings.py`; [What changed in settings, startup and the commands](changes/startup-and-commands.md)).

A model that declares no primary key and has no parent, such as journal's Entry, is given one, of the class that `DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD` names unless its application names another (`django/db/models/options.py:Options._get_default_pk_class`).
6.0 changed the setting's default from `AutoField` to `BigAutoField`, and nothing warns; the line for 5.2.17 is the old key (`django/conf/global_settings.py`):

A project upgraded to 6.0 that never named the class finds the key of each such model now a `BigAutoField`, and makemigrations writes an `AlterField` for each (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_fields`).
Since 3.2 the system check models.W042 had warned of each such model in a project that did not set `DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD`; 6.0 removed it (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`, `docs/ref/checks.txt`).

At this commit `MiddlewareMixin`, the base class of nearly all Django's own middleware, lives in `django.middleware`, and its old module's `__getattr__` hands the class to an old import with a warning (`django/utils/deprecation.py:__getattr__`).

5.2 deprecated `login` given no user, which then logged in the request's user, and 6.1, the Y.1 that ends what the long-term 5.2 deprecated, removed the fallback (`docs/releases/5.2.txt`, `django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:login`).
